title: Transient per-route / per-org accounting discrepancy causing under/over-charging on retries
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Intermittent mismatches observed between token usage reported on billing ledgers and what the rate-enforcer metrics indicate. The issue appears when requests traverse the multi-layer enforcement stack (per-key -> per-route -> per-org) and are retried or routed to a fallback model variant. Symptoms include transient under-charging (missing tokens) followed by corrective spikes when background reconciler runs, and in other cases double-counting when a request is replayed after a soft-failure. This ticket scopes investigation, mitigation, and a permanent fix for the enforcement path and reconciliation logic.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use org X with per-org quota and a per-route SLO configured (low burst window).
2) Send a batch of requests that trigger route fallback (primary model returns 503, fallback used).
3) Introduce a client-side retry at the SDK layer with idempotency disabled for 10% of requests.
4) Observe /api/v1/usage and billing ledger vs rate-enforcer metrics around event timestamps (10s windows).
impact: Customer-facing billing variance: some customers see short-lived under-billing then sudden reconciliation corrections; internal accounting alerts for quota exhaustion can be suppressed or fired incorrectly. Affects hosted API users and Dedicated customers with strict org-level quotas. Estimated surface: ~0.5% of requests in mixed-retry traffic patterns; high severity due to billing correctness implications.
root_cause: Preliminary hypothesis: race between (A) token debit path used by per-route enforcer and (B) async write to the ledger that deduplicates by request_id. When a retry occurs before the ledger write is durable, the per-key/per-route enforcer may proceed without seeing the pending write and either allow extra tokens or skip debit depending on path. Additionally, fallback routing spawns a synthetic request record that is not normalized against the original request_id, causing duplicate ledger entries.
proposed_solution: Short term: disable client-side automatic retries for affected SDK versions and roll out a server-side idempotency guard for 72 hours to reduce variance.
Medium term: ensure the enforcer uses a single canonical debit operation with strong request_id deduplication (persist-before-debit or transactional ledger write + commit signal).

Long term: rework fallback routing to carry original request_id and add a deterministic reconciliation window that is bounded and emits compensating events instead of best-effort fixes. Add unit/integration test harness that simulates retry/fallback race scenarios.
rollout_plan: 1) Patch: server-side idempotency guard behind feature flag -> deploy to staging (canary).
2) Run synthetic load tests simulating retry/fallback patterns, validate ledger vs enforcer counts on staging dashboard.
3) Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic for orgs with >P1 plans for 48h with increased observability.
4) Full rollout + post-deploy reconciliation job if variance persists.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Chen: Initial triage; added synthetic repro harness. Observed duplicated ledger rows when fallback does not propagate request_id.
2026-03-04 - Luca Moretti: Confirmed race window ~200-400ms between ledger write and enforcer debit under high concurrency. Instrumented timings in staging run.
2026-03-06 - PM Aisha Patel: Customer-communications drafted; recommended temporary quota soft-lock to avoid over-serving during canary.
2026-03-08 - Security review (Ivan Petrov): No additional data-sensitivity concerns; ensure request_id propagation doesn't expose PII in logs.
2026-03-10 - Engineering review: Decided to implement persist-before-debit pattern with idempotency key stored in strongly-consistent store (etcd) for canonicalization.
2026-03-11 - QA (Nora Kim): Running integration tests across dedicated and hosted configurations; seeing reduced variance in 3/4 scenarios, investigating edge case with burst autoscaling.
